Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroDef Corporation Q3 FY2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, participants are required to use their handset for optimal sound quality. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroDef Corporation's Q3 FY2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroDef Corporation delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, I'll highlight our progress in revenue growth by segment, the recovery in commercial aircraft deliveries, R&D investments in next-generation platforms, drivers of our aftermarket performance, and free cash flow generation.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to establish leadership in next-generation air dominance for the U.S. Air Force and allies. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 sustainment and hypersonic weapons, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with improving delivery rates.

Let me start with revenue by segment. In Q3, consolidated revenues reached $7.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with standout growth in commercial aerospace at 28% driven by OEM deliveries and aftermarket pull-through. Defense grew 6% on F-35 lots and missile programs, while services rose 11% from MRO demand. Year-to-date, we're at $26.4 billion, up 14%, with a book-to-bill of 1.3x and a $185 billion backlog providing clear visibility.

Commercial aircraft deliveries are ramping meaningfully, with 185 units in the quarter across narrowbody and widebody platforms, putting us on pace for strong full-year results as air traffic surpasses pre-pandemic levels. Aftermarket performance is equally robust, fueled by higher fleet utilization at 3.8 block hours per day and normalized maintenance cycles, generating high-margin recurring revenue.

On the innovation front, our R&D efforts are advancing hypersonics, space architectures, and autonomy, positioning us for the $1.2 trillion A&D market opportunity through 2030. And underpinning all this is our free cash flow engine, delivering $1.4 billion in the quarter.

I'll now turn it over to Michael for the detailed financials.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Johnathan. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $7.2 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.15, reflecting strong operational execution. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at $26.8 to $27.3 billion in revenue and $5.8 to $6.3 billion in free cash flow. We are actively managing our costs amid inflation pressures and investing in key growth initiatives like capacity expansion and digital transformation. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include a gross margin of 22.5%, operating income of $1.8 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion.

Diving deeper into revenue by segment, commercial aerospace led with Q3 revenues of $3.1 billion, up 28% year-over-year, and year-to-date $11.5 billion, up 22%. This was powered by 185 widebody and narrowbody deliveries, including next-gen platforms optimized for sustainable aviation fuels, with strong orders from Asia-Pacific carriers. We've resolved titanium supply issues through dual-sourcing with U.S. and Japanese suppliers, boosting production throughput by 18% using digital thread tools like Siemens NX. North America drove 55% of growth via Delta and United modernizations, Europe 35% from Ryanair and Lufthansa, and Asia-Pacific a stellar 45% from IndiGo and Chinese lessors. We're guiding mid-teens growth for FY2024 with 750 deliveries and a 1.4x book-to-bill.

Defense delivered Q3 revenues of $2.8 billion, up 6%, and year-to-date $10.2 billion, up 8%, supported by DoD budgets and international demand. Highlights included $450 million in F-35 Lot 15 deliveries with Block 4 avionics upgrades using gallium nitride tech, and 120 HIMARS launchers for Ukraine aid. Hypersonics added $1.8 billion year-to-date from ARRW and Blackbird II prototypes. Missile defense contributed $2.5 billion for Patriot interceptors to Saudi Arabia and Poland. U.S. was 60% of the segment, EMEA up 25% on NATO aid, and Indo-Pacific 15% via AUKUS. Backlog stands at $110 billion with modular open systems architecture de-risking execution; we expect 7-9% growth next year.

Services hit Q3 revenues of $1.3 billion, up 11%, and year-to-date $5.1 billion, up 16%, at 22% operating margins. Engine overhauls for CFM LEAP variants spiked 25%, with additive manufacturing cutting turnaround by 30%. F-16 upgrades for Slovakia and Taiwan added strength. MRO hubs in Singapore and Dubai grew 20%, U.S. C-130J sustainment $800 million. Our AeroDef ONE platform boosts utilization to 92%, with 40% from performance-based logistics. We see 12-15% growth ahead on a $25 billion backlog.

Turning to commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory, in Q3 we delivered 142 units, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, on track for 550-600 full-year amid 4% above-2019 passenger traffic. Narrowbodies were 78% at 112 units, mostly 737 MAX, widebodies 30 including 787s and 777X milestones. Backlog-to-sales is 12.5 years on $400 billion. Orders included 220 gross, with narrowbody strength from Zipair and Qantas. North America 42%, Asia-Pacific 35% via ANA and IndiGo's 500-unit framework, Europe 15%, Middle East/LATAM 8%. Renton factory digital twins cut 737 build times 22%, Everett autokey reduced 787 defects 35%. Dual-sourced titanium, engine forward-furnishing $500 million. All deliveries SAF-compatible, with A&D synergies like F-35 composites accelerating certs. Inventory down 5% to $28 billion, pricing up 4%. FY2025 outlook 720-780 units.

Aftermarket performance drivers are fleet utilization and maintenance cycles. Q3 aftermarket generated $2.8 billion, up 18%, 42% of sales, EBITDA margins 28.2%. Fleet utilization hit 3.8 block hours/day, up 19%, with 82% load factors. Commercial narrowbodies over 4,000 annual hours, defense F-35/F-18 at 92%. Americas 55% share up 22%, EMEA 16%, APAC 25% up 25%. Maintenance visits up 14%, MTBHV extended 15% on LEAP engines to 25,000 cycles. F-35 sustainment cut groundings 22%. StratOS AI platform covers 70% MRO, cutting removals 30%, dispatch 99.5%. Stocked rotables halved lead times. Partnerships with Boeing/Lockheed for $1.2 billion new agreements. Targeting 20% CAGR, with China JV for C919 checks.

Now, on free cash flow generation and utilization—one of our core strengths in this long-cycle sector. Q3 FCF was $1.4 billion, year-to-date $4.2 billion, up 28%, strongest in five years. Operating cash flow $2.1 billion at 95% conversion on $1.8 billion adjusted profit. Accelerated collections on F-35 sustainment and JADC2, invoicing $850 million early. Capex $650 million or 4.2% of sales: 40% Fort Worth F-35 expansion for Lot 15+, 30% Huntsville Additive Center cutting titanium times 35%, CapEx per unit 22%. U.S. 72% of YTD FCF at $3.0 billion on NDAA $886 billion, hypersonics backlog $2.5 billion. Europe $650 million up 45% on F-35 from Finland/Poland, AEGIS. Asia-Pacific $550 million from P-8s, KF-21 delays. TTM FCF yield 8.2% vs. peers 6.1%. $168 billion backlog, 65% in 24 months, margins up 120 bps to 12.4%. ERP 2.0 cut DSO to 42 days.

Utilization: $3.1 billion returned YTD—$1.2 billion dividends at $1.28/share (3.2% yield, 11th increase), $1.9 billion repurchases retiring 4.2% shares at $285 avg, boosting EPS 8%, targeting 50-60% payout. Reduced net debt $1.1 billion to $12.4 billion, leverage 1.8x. $600 million internal R&D for hypersonic tunnels, CCA software. $850 million tuck-in M&A like $425 million directed-energy acquisition. $200 million multi-sourcing titanium, $150 million Venture Studio for space startups. FY guidance $5.8-6.3 billion, Q4 from LRASM/SATCOM. $25 billion liquidity buffers risks.

On R&D investment in next-gen platforms, FY2023 spend $2.18 billion or 8.3% of revenues, up 15%, targeting 9-10%. Outpaces industry 6.5%. NGAD/CCA 42% ($915 million): digital twin MBSE cut design 25%, two X-planes early, AI autonomy, $450 million DARPA CRAD, export to AUKUS. Hypersonics 25% ($545 million): Mach 5+ scramjet TRL 7, Hermeus partnership, $1.2 billion backlog. Space 18% ($392 million): LEO constellations, quantum links on Pathfinder-7, NRO talks. Directed energy/autonomy 15% ($327 million): 300 kW lasers, AI for JADC2, Anduril dual-use. 65% USG, 35% international. 4:1 ROI, $4.2 billion bookings. FY2024 $2.4-2.5 billion.

Gross margin expansion and FCF strength reflect our balanced portfolio.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 and 737 MAX. We are investing in automation and digital technologies, including additive manufacturing centers and AI predictive maintenance, to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and shorten lead times by up to 35%. Our Fort Worth and Renton facilities are ramping sustainably, with digital twins optimizing flows and dual-sourcing mitigating geopolitical risks. Retention at 98% supports this, despite sector attrition.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. From a technology perspective, our R&D is delivering flight-qualified prototypes in hypersonics, NGAD loyal wingmen, and space-resilient architectures. Digital engineering and open mission systems are compressing cycles and lowering costs, with early wins in CCA demonstrators and scramjet inlets. We're partnering across DoD, DARPA, and international allies to lead in contested domains.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, participants may ask questions by pressing star then one on their touchtone phone. Our first question comes from David Larsen with Bernstein. Please go ahead.

David Larsen:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory, especially with widebody ramps?

Johnathan Hale:
Certainly, David. As Michael detailed, Q3 deliveries of 142 units put us on track for 550-600 annually, with narrowbodies leading at 78%. Widebodies at 30 units face engine and fuselage constraints, but digital twins at Everett have cut 787 defects 35%, targeting 5/month. Backlog $400 billion, orders strong in Asia-Pacific like IndiGo's framework. Supply chain dual-sourcing and A&D tech transfers like stealth composites position us for 720-780 in 2025, outpacing peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Marie Duval with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Marie Duval:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about free cash flow utilization, particularly M&A and debt reduction plans?

Michael Reynolds:
Marie, great question. YTD FCF of $4.2 billion has enabled $3.1 billion shareholder returns—dividends up to $1.28/share and $1.9 billion buybacks—plus $1.1 billion debt paydown to 1.8x leverage. We've done tuck-ins like the $425 million directed-energy deal for counter-drone tech, $600 million internal R&D, and supply chain resilience investments. $850 million earmarked for more M&A targeting space and hypersonics convergence, with $25 billion liquidity for flexibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Regarding the R&D investments in next-generation platforms like NGAD and hypersonics—what's the pipeline look like?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Raj, our $2.18 billion FY2023 R&D, 8.3% of sales, focuses on high-ROI areas. NGAD/CCA at $915 million delivered X-planes early via MBSE, positioning for $20 billion PEN tranche and AUKUS exports. Hypersonics $545 million hit TRL 7 on scramjets, $1.2 billion backlog. Space proliferated LEO and quantum links, directed energy 300 kW lasers. FY2024 guidance $2.4-2.5 billion for B-21 and GCAP pursuits. Historical 4:1 returns validate this.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across commercial recovery, defense leadership, services growth, R&D breakthroughs, and FCF discipline.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 FY2023 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
